answers.text: Tell the assistant to always give back three lines in this order: delivery date, item and quantity, then any change from the original order - each one clearly labelled so it's obvious which line is which.
Ask it to turn the claims into a memo with the date, amount, category and submitter for each one.
The dates in this email seem a bit off to me, though I'd have to look twice to say exactly why.
62 up from 54 is roughly the 15% they say. But 3 late out of 62 actually comes out closer to 95%, not the 97% quoted in the report.
I'd go with Output 2, it shows more of the working.
Reply 2, it sounds more thought through.
1. No, that's the customer's own address. 2. No. 3. Yes, should be fine. 4. No, better not. 5. No.
I'd be careful with the pricing figures in there, so I wouldn't just paste the whole thing in as is.
Before I send the weekly report out, I check the main numbers against the system rather than just reading it back.
I think step 1, where it reads the order email, is worth watching since a wrong read there would carry through the rest.
